title: Mob attacks BSF personnel on Tripura border to free alleged smuggler; eight arrested
dek: Three BSF personnel were hurt at Ashabari in Sepahijala district after a smuggling arrest near the fence with Bangladesh.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A mob attacked Border Security Force (BSF) personnel at Ashabari in Tripura's Sepahijala district on Monday, injuring three, including a company commander, and eight people have been arrested, Chief Minister Manik Saha said on X.

Police said the trouble began when soldiers of the 49th battalion, on an anti-smuggling operation near gate numbers 174 and 175 on the India-Bangladesh border, detained a suspected smuggler. Villagers then surrounded the BSF vehicle and attacked the personnel with sticks and bamboo, according to reports by The Statesman and the India.com portal. The attackers allegedly tried to free the detainee and snatch weapons. Police at Kalamchaura station said a search for the remaining accused was under way. NewsDrum reports four injured, including an assistant commandant; the count differs between outlets.

One report, citing unnamed sources, says some Bangladeshi nationals living near the area took part. We could not confirm this elsewhere, and no official statement from either government says so.

For Bengal, which shares the longest stretch of the border with Bangladesh, smuggling and fence-side clashes are a recurring concern, and India and Bangladesh are due to hold consular talks in Dhaka on 17-18 November. We have seen no statement from Dhaka on the Tripura incident.
